title: lateinit and lazy
context: When would you use lateinit and when would you use lazy?

refs.title: Atomic Kotlin (book) by Bruce Eckel & Svetlana Isakova

answer: lateinit lets a non-null var be assigned after construction, typically by a framework or a setup method. It works only for non-primitive types, and reading it before assignment throws UninitializedPropertyAccessException. lazy computes a val once, on first access, and then caches it. By default it is thread-safe, with a lock. Use lazy for expensive values that may never be needed, and lateinit when a dependency is injected later. Check with `::prop.isInitialized` before reading a lateinit property if the value may be missing.

points.title: Read before write
points.why: Reading an uninitialized lateinit property throws at run time.

points.title: Lazy caches once
points.why: lazy runs its initializer on first use and then reuses the value.
